findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\lunarOrbit-4k.png, lowOrbit-4k.png, translunar-4k.png, reentry-4k.png, failed-4k.png, attitude-lowOrbit-4k.png, entry-highg-4k.png and their 720p twins; bright-reentry-720p.png (navball rim at level attitude)
findings.defect: At any attitude except pole-on, the numerals at the left and right rim of the ball fade across the glyph, and the faded part becomes a blurred copy of the numeral, not clean paint. In lunarOrbit-4k, '150' at the right rim reads '15' and then a soft smear. The upper-right '50' (x 2000-2090, y 1675-1730) is a sharp '5' beside a smudged '0', and the upper-left '60' is a pale blur next to the window reflection. The bottom-left '-60' is a fragment. In lowOrbit-4k, '30' reads '3' plus a smear and '-20' reads '-2'. At 720p these are 3 to 5 px grey crumbs: a lone '7', '3' and '-2' at the right rim of lowOrbit-720p and bright-reentry-720p. Markers fade the same way. In attitude-lowOrbit-4k the normal marker at the right rim is drawn at about half alpha, a translucent violet ghost over the '150' numeral. Round 3 says 'a numeral never ends cut in half'. That holds pole-on but not at level attitude, which is most of a mission.
findings.realReference: The FDAI in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg: ball markings stay crisp right up to the case mask and pass under it cleanly. Nothing is half-dissolved or smeared at the edge of the window. On KSP's navball the rim numerals are foreshortened but sharp.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/navball/navballShader.ts lines 135-141: `paint = mix(bg, albedo, inkVisible)`, where `bg` is the same inked texture sampled with 12x gradients. That coarse mip still holds the numerals smeared out, so fading toward it leaves a blurred ghost. `lipFade = 1 - smoothstep(lip - 0.075, lip - 0.012, r)` is evaluated per pixel, so the fade boundary runs through a glyph. In vsMarker (lines 201-205), `smoothstep(w - 0.05, w + 0.02, |pos|)` draws a marker whose centre is at lip - 0.02 at about 55 % alpha.
findings.fixDirection: Fade toward an ink-free background, not a mip of the inked texture: the paint colour by pitch sign, or a second ink-free texture. Decide each numeral's visibility per label, not per pixel. One way is a per-label fade channel in the texture, written from the label anchor's polar angle. Another is to draw the numerals as instanced glyphs like the markers, hidden as a whole once their centre passes about 0.88 R. Give markers full strength until they are under the lip, with at most a 1 to 2 degree fade. Re-shoot lunarOrbit-4k and crop both rims: every visible numeral should be either whole or absent.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\mfd-pages-4k.png, mfd-pages-native.png, mfd-pages-hover-4k.png (ORB page, Moon); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\mfd-pages-native-reentry.png (ORB page, Earth)
findings.defect: The body on the orbit page is two flat tones split by a ruled edge, and the light along the terminator does not add up. In mfd-pages-4k, column x = 2180 across the Moon: the night side is (46,45,42). It jumps to (95,93,89) within 2 px at y = 562, then brightens to (143,140,134) toward the sub-solar point. So the ground where the sun stands on the horizon is drawn at two thirds of peak brightness, and the day side has a hard 2 : 1 step against the night side. On the Earth the terminator is a straight 1 px diagonal with no twilight band. The disc carries no surface detail (no maria, no land, no cloud), so it reads as a cut-paper two-tone ball. This is the residual of the round-1 photo minor: the terminator was added, but its shading is wrong.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\moon-surface\earthrise-a8.jpg: the Earth's day side darkens continuously toward its terminator, with no bright band against the night side. Lunar photographs in the same folder show the lit regolith falling to dark at the terminator (low sun, long shadows), never a bright edge.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/mfd/mfdPainter.ts lines 975-980 (drawBodyDisc). The day fill is a linear gradient from 1.35 x the mean colour at the sub-solar limb to 0.42 x at the terminator, clipped by a hard path. The night fill is 0.09 x (line 956), so the edge is a step from 0.42 to 0.09 with no falloff, and the gradient is linear in screen distance rather than in the cosine of the incidence angle.
findings.fixDirection: Shade the day side by the cosine of the incidence angle per pixel, so it reaches night level at the terminator. For a disc drawn on a canvas, a radial gradient centred on the projected sub-solar point and ending at the terminator works. Soften the edge over 1 to 2 % of R, more on bodies with an atmosphere (twilight). A few low-contrast blotches from a fixed per-body seed (no coastline tables needed) would also stop the disc reading as flat. Re-shoot and check that the brightness across the terminator falls within 10 levels of the night side.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\entry-highg-720p.png and entry-highg-4k.png against reentry-720p.png, reentry-4k.png and failed-720p.png (same entry scene, with and without a g-dose)
findings.defect: When the G DOSE line appears, the gauge panel grows upward and the instrument moves. In reentry-720p the gauge panel's top edge is at y = 596. In entry-highg-720p it is at y = 573, and both tubes, their scales and the value row sit 23 px higher (69 px at 4K). The hand-off says the line shows only while there is a dose, so the throttle and g tubes jump the moment the first dose builds up (in a real entry, exactly when the pilot is watching the g tube) and jump back if it clears. This is layout pop in the one instrument that must not move.
findings.realReference: Fixed instrument faces: the tape gauges on the Apollo panel (C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg) and the gauge strips of shipped flight HUDs keep each scale in a fixed place. Indicators that appear late take reserved space or overlay it.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts line 351: `.gauges .doseline` adds a fourth grid row (`grid-row: 4`) of 1.3em + 0.35u to a bottom-anchored panel. Round 3 removed the reserved slot so the empty space would disappear.
findings.fixDirection: Keep the dose line's height reserved whenever the vessel is in an atmosphere or under acceleration, with a dim 'G DOSE 0 %' rather than nothing. Or anchor the panel's tube rows and let the dose line extend downward into the bottom margin. Add a layout assertion that the g tube's bounding box is the same in reentry and entry-highg.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\ascent-4k.png, ascent-720p.png, bright-ascent-720p.png, warp-refused.png (ORBIT panel); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\mfd-pages-native-reentry.png, mfd-pages-4k.png (ENT page gauge headers)
findings.defect: Typographic misalignment introduced by the round-3 overflow fix. In the suborbital orbit panel, APOAPSIS '15.5 km' ends at x ~ 990 (4K) while PERIAPSIS '-6 361.1 km' ends at the panel edge, x ~ 1368. The two values of one two-row table have different right edges, so the apoapsis value floats in the middle with its time 'T- 0:35' beside it. This shows in every ascent picture. Smaller: on the MFD ENT page the G DOSE gauge header is a bare '0.0', while its neighbours carry units ('4.50 g', '80 %', '55 %').
findings.realReference: Shipped data panels and real display pages (the readout columns of C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\soyuz-ms20-descent-module.jpg's display) keep one right-aligned value column per table and drop or blank the secondary column rather than letting one value spill into it.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts lines 363-366: `.apsis` is `auto 1fr auto`, and `.apsis.wide .val { grid-column: 2 / 4 }` lets only the wide row's value span the time column. The ENT gauge header in src/ui/mfd/mfdPainter.ts formats the dose without a unit.
findings.fixDirection: When any apsis row is wide, render both rows wide: values right-aligned to the panel edge, with times dropped or moved below. Or keep the time column and shorten the periapsis to '-6 361 km'. Header the dose gauge '0.0 g·s' or as a share ('0 %'), as on the HUD dose line.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\lunarSurface-720p.png, lunarSurface-4k.png, terrain-pending-720p.png, translunar-720p.png, lunarOrbit-720p.png, lowOrbit-720p.png, cockpit-lowOrbit-720p.png (ACTIVE tile)
findings.defect: The green ACTIVE tile is titled with its stage's trigger event, so the HUD states something that is not happening. Landed on the Moon, it reads 'M-3 separation · ACTIVE · Δv 554 m/s' while the resources panel directly below says 'Lander 22 %'. In low orbit it reads 'M-2 separation · ACTIVE' over 'M-2 upper stage 34 %'. In the ascent it reads 'Launch · ACTIVE'. 'Separation ACTIVE' reads as a separation in progress, and the burning stage's name never matches the tank group drained beside it.
findings.realReference: Propulsion and sequencer displays name the engine or stage that is burning, and KSP's staging stack shows the parts of the active stage (engine and tank icons), not the decoupler event that lit them.
findings.likelyCause: src/ui/hud/hud.ts lines 786-792 (fullTile) use the StageInfo name for both roles. For the next stage that name is the right label (what Space will do). For the active stage it is the event that already happened.
findings.fixDirection: Title the active tile by what is burning: the engine or tank group the stage owns, for example 'Lander descent' or 'M-2 upper stage', from the stage's parts or the resource group. Keep the event name only on the next tile. Assert in the lunar-surface spec that the active tile's title matches the drained resource group's name.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\reentry-4k.png, failed-4k.png, entry-highg-4k.png (backdrop horizon at y = 640); pad-720p.png, ascent-720p.png, chutes-720p.png, retrograde-hold-720p.png, warp-refused.png (sea grid); lunarSurface-720p.png, lunarOrbit-4k.png (Moon); map-lowOrbit-720p.png; warp-refused.png (toast); cockpit-cabin-lowOrbit-720p.png and -4k.png
findings.defect: Evidence, not a HUD fault: every picture of the package is shot over lab placeholder art that has visible rendering faults of its own. On the reentry backdrop a ruled horizontal line runs the full width at y = 640 (4K), luminance 8 to 50 in one pixel, with stars printed inside the atmosphere band below it. The sea is a flat plane with a visible white grid lattice. The Moon is a flat grey faceted plane, the rocket a grey cylinder, and the map view's Earth a flat disc with a faint grid and no orbit. So the HUD has never been judged over the real renderer's highlights, bloom, sun or cloud tops. Two pictures misreport the HUD's steady state. warp-refused.png is captured mid fade-in, so the rocket shows through the toast, 20 levels in the text row. The cabin composite pairs a HUD clock of T+ 00:00:00 with the cabin's 00:00:05 and a cabin MFD at roll -90° that matches no HUD state.
findings.realReference: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\earth-orbit-clouds\limb-panorama.jpg: a curved, graded limb with no ruled line and no stars inside the airglow band. The photographs in out/qa/ref/launch-pad and out/qa/ref/reentry-chutes are what the HUD will sit over in the shipped game.
findings.likelyCause: labs/flight-ui/backdrop.ts draws a stand-in scene (lab only, by design). tests/browser/flight-ui/controls.spec.ts lines 175-178 save warp-refused after waitFrames(5), inside the 160 ms `hud-toast-in` animation (src/ui/hud/hudStyles.ts line 198). The cabin view is a still of the cockpit package's render (out/screens/cockpit/perf-1440p-leo-seat.png) under a live HUD from a different state.
findings.fixDirection: Shoot at least the low-orbit, ascent and lunar-surface HUD views over stills of the real renderer (as the cabin view already does with the cockpit package's render), or over the integration once it exists. Fix the backdrop's horizon (a graded limb, no stars below it) or replace the backdrop with those stills. Wait for the toast's animationend before warp-refused is saved. Drive the lab's clock and attitude to the still's state for the cabin composite.
